text: The two versioned tables, the reference version registry, the read service, the load and approve operations and the cache stay with P3 rwb-case under the R-PREC default ruling; the platform library reads them through the rwb-case contract and owns no table, no schema and no migration.
why: Template and Rules section R3 puts parameters and reference data with P3 rwb-case by default ruling, and the Ownership Map assigns reference_version, reference_row and lov_value to P3; the platform library is not one of the 19 services and cannot own a schema, so the only consistent reading is that it reads and does not store.
read: Template and Rules section R3 default rulings (parameters and reference data, E1-042 and E1-043, to P3 rwb-case); Ownership Map v1 entries reference_version, reference_row and lov_value (owner P3); Plan Appendix R DP-07
applied_in: RWB-PLT-E1043-APP sections 2, 11, 12.7 and 19; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON sections 2, 12.7 and 19
confirm: rwb-case owner and platform team at the wave 0 design gate
impact: Fixes which stories own the tables and the operations; no business value changes and no legacy acceptance criterion moves

text: The client keeps the legacy read behaviour: the approved version with the latest valid from on or before the business date, a cache whose time to live is a catalog entry read through the parameters client, one log line per table read with the table code, the version number and the business date, and a typed exception when no approved version applies.
why: The legacy story fixes the read rule, the log line and the refusal, and no target source replaces them; the only change the target forces is where the time to live comes from, which is the rwb-case parameter catalog under DP-06 instead of the monolith configuration service.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-043 sections 4, 8 BR3, BR7 and BR9, 9 and 13 (refdata.cache.ttl-seconds = 300, assumed; DL11); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 20; Plan DP-06 and DP-07
applied_in: RWB-PLT-E1043-APP sections 3, 4, 7, 8 and 13; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON sections 12.2 and 13
confirm: rwb-case owner and platform team at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes the read rule, the log fields, the cache and the refusal of the library; the value 300 is the legacy default and stays configuration

text: A version change reaches a consumer by cache expiry, because the legacy design publishes no event for a version change and this run invents none; a later owner event would be consumed through the inbox library and would raise the client contract to a new version.
why: Legacy section 12 states that no events are published and the outbox carries none for the story, and Architecture v5 slide 20 lists no reference event among the cache-refresh events of a service; inventing one would add an event type that no owner publishes.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (no events published; the outbox carries none); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 20; Plan DP-09 and DP-14
applied_in: RWB-PLT-E1043-APP sections 4, 8, 12.3, 12.4 and 13; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON sections 12.4, 17 and 19
confirm: rwb-case owner and event platform team at the contract freeze
impact: No event, topic or inbox subscription is added for reference data; the refresh is the cache expiry

text: The client contract is published as one versioned artefact at major version 1, carrying the records of the legacy contract (ReferenceDataClient, ReferenceVersion, VersionedRows and NoVersionInForceException) and the twelve reference table codes, with a breaking change raising version 2 and deprecating version 1.
why: The legacy interfaces and records are the only agreed shapes and no target source redefines them; publishing them as one artefact with a version is what lets 19 services pin a contract and run a drift test, which Architecture v5 slide 11 requires of every build.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (published interfaces and records); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (contract-first, contract tests in every build); Template and Rules section R5.4 class C
confirm: Platform contract owner and the consuming service teams at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes the published surface and the deprecation rule; the artefact coordinates stay with the platform library baseline

text: The rule tables stay with P7 rwb-decision and the holiday calendar with ACE and P1 rwb-source-data, so the client serves neither; the kit boundary is proved in a contract test rather than described in prose only.
why: The Ownership Map keeps rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case with P7 and the rule registry central under the Temporal and Drools design, while the holiday calendar is ACE data read through v_ace_holiday by P1; a client that served either would break DP-04, DP-05 and DP-01.
